paper_title: $A'$ view of the sunrise: Boosting helioscopes with angular information
notes: Paper derives new 90% CL exclusion limits on dark photon kinetic mixing from Hinode XRT calibration darks (helioscope-style, sensitive ~1e-2 eV to keV, kink at ~3e-2 eV) and a 2012 solar eclipse image (light-shining-through-the-Moon, extends sensitivity down to ~2e-6 eV kink mass). Full limit curves are shown only in figures 5 and 8; no numerical table is provided. Extracted points come from text: Table 1 quotes darks sensitivity eps~1e-9 and eclipse eps~4e-8 at m=1 eV; benchmark points near the exclusion limit (radial+spectral analysis, no background subtraction) are eps=6.1e-11 at 400 eV, eps=1.2e-10 at 15 eV. The best (data-driven background subtracted) darks limit is somewhat stronger than these benchmarks. Fourth data point [1 eV, 4e-8] is the ECLIPSE limit (separate curve from darks). No DM density assumed - constraint from solar dark photon production, not a DM halo search.
